question.problem: The third and fourth terms of an arithmetic sequence are $-60$ and $-76,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms ${a}_{3}=-60$ and ${a}_{4}=-76$ are consecutive, we can subtract to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{4}-{a}_{3} \\  & =-76-(-60) \\  & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{3}=-60,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{3}$ is $2$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & ={a}_{1}+2d \\ -60 & ={a}_{1}+2(-16) \\ -60 & ={a}_{1}-32 \\ -28 & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

So the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-28+(n-1)(-16) \\  & =-28-16n+16 \\  & =-16n-12\end{aligned}
$$
